learning_objective: 🔬 Grab a microscope and explore the internal architecture of plants, discovering how cells group together to form complex tissues!

key_vocabulary.hindi_meaning: शारीरिकी (जीवों की आंतरिक संरचना का अध्ययन)
विभज्योतक (लगातार विभाजित होने वाली कोशिकाओं का समूह)

main_concepts.simple_explanation: These are the active growth regions of a plant. Apical meristems occur at the tips of roots and shoots (primary growth/length). Lateral meristems (like cambium) occur on the sides and increase the girth/thickness of the plant (secondary growth).

Cells that have stopped dividing. Simple permanent tissues are made of one cell type (Parenchyma for storage, Collenchyma for flexible support, Sclerenchyma for rigid, dead support). Complex tissues have multiple cell types working together (Xylem and Phloem).
Plants have 3 main systems: 1. Epidermal (outer protective layer with stomata and root hairs), 2. Ground (the bulk of the plant body, mostly parenchyma), and 3. Vascular (xylem and phloem bundles).

main_concepts.concept_title: 🔍 Anatomy of Dicot vs. Monocot Stem
main_concepts.simple_explanation: In Dicot stems, vascular bundles are arranged in a neat ring and contain cambium (open, allowing secondary growth). In Monocot stems, vascular bundles are scattered everywhere and lack cambium (closed, so grass doesn't grow into thick wooden trunks).
Mostly seen in dicot roots and stems. The vascular cambium produces secondary xylem inwards (which we call 'wood') and secondary phloem outwards. Cork cambium produces protective bark on the outside.

fun_activity.title: 🌳 Read the Tree Rings
fun_activity.instructions: When a tree is cut, you can see rings in the wood. These are formed by the vascular cambium making different sized xylem vessels in Spring (wide, light wood) vs. Autumn (narrow, dark wood). One light + one dark ring = 1 year of the tree's life!

exam_tips: 📌 Xylem strictly flows in one direction (roots to leaves), while Phloem can transport food bi-directionally (leaves to roots, or storage organs to growing buds).
📌 Remember the difference in root anatomy: Dicot roots have fewer xylem bundles (diarch to hexarch), while Monocot roots are polyarch (more than 6 xylem bundles) with a large central pith.
📌 Bulliform cells in monocot leaves (like grasses) help the leaf curl inwards during water stress to minimize water loss.
quick_recap: ⭐ Parenchyma is the most abundant simple tissue, mainly involved in photosynthesis, storage, and secretion.
⭐ Stomata are pores in the epidermis flanked by guard cells (bean-shaped in dicots, dumbbell-shaped in monocots).
⭐ Heartwood is the dead, dark central wood that provides mechanical support, while sapwood is the outer, lighter wood that conducts water.
